answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable delay function: repeated modular squarings depend on the previous result, so one chain cannot be shortcut by distributing its steps across GPUs. An attacker may run clone chains in parallel, but each still consumes sequential time and hardware, making mass identity creation costly. Wesolowski proofs let verifiers check completion efficiently; copper, kernel, and violet are merely labels, not ways around the delay.
